They were measured identical on origin/main in a worktree and are pre-existing debt outside this changeset's scope. None was fixed, because widening the PR to chase them is the accretion this session spent 6,716 lines reversing.

bias_direction: I am biased toward the map being right, because I commissioned the surveys that produced it, adjudicated their output, and then wrote the file — so every check on it was a check I thought to run. The third adversarial pass demonstrates the cost concretely: it found that my own correction of the reader counts used the same defective instrument as the claim it corrected. I am also biased toward reporting the refusal of the A-18 cell as a success, because refusing is cheaper than determining and produces an artifact that cannot be falsified by later evidence. Against that, a bias the other way: I had a standing incentive to reach a green PR and stop, and every additional break found delayed it, so treat the absence of breaks 27 and 28 as weak evidence rather than as coverage.
independent_reviewer_counterclaim: A reviewer could say this session is the pathology it diagnoses. It was commissioned to walk the pipeline and author one cell; it authored none, added a 400-line governance document that nothing reads, and closed with more open owner-gated questions than it opened with. Thirty-one commits and zero rows of evidence. The stronger form: the map is descriptive, self-declares that no code consumes it, and hardcodes volatile facts that CLAUDE.md section 2b says will drift — so by the repository's own doctrine it is prose about the machine rather than machine, and prose about the machine is what D-2 says must never be the body. The counter is that the cull removed 6,716 lines against 400 added, and that BRK-20 and BRK-26 are defects in the write path the next determination would have used, so the walk did carry something back. But a reviewer is entitled to answer that a map which nothing reads is a plan for a sequencer, not a sequencer, and that this project has never been short of plans.
